question.text: What will be the average performance on ANIMA for AI models released between June 2026 and June 2027?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the average "overall mean score" of all AI models that have been released after May 31, 2026 and before July 1, 2027 and been evaluated by [ANIMA](https://compassionbench.com/ahb).

Only the models that are present on the leaderboard as of September 1, 2027 will count for the purposes of this question.
question.fine_print: If ANIMA changes its scoring methodology such that it is incompatible with the current scores (e.g., scoring changes so as not to be a percentage) then this question will be **annulled**. However, if the scoring methodology is modified to include more questions in the dataset or evaluates more dimensions without changing the final metric (e.g., it remains as a percentage) this will not result in this question being **annulled**.

# ANIMA (CompassionBench) research brief, as of 2026-11-05

The most important finding: I could not read the leaderboard itself, and ANIMA is now a "legacy" board that may get few or no new models. Every attempt to fetch compassionbench.com returned HTTP 403, and the Wayback Machine was also blocked. I could not confirm which models released since June 2026 are listed, or what they scored.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-05: compassionbench.com/ahb, /anima and the home page all returned 403. I have no current leaderboard value. The question background says GPT-5.5 led at 74.0 on 2026-05-12, but I could not verify that. [compassionbench](https://compassionbench.com/ahb)
- Current (undated): the site run by CaML (Compassion in Machine Learning) says the leaderboard is "led by our current benchmarks TAC, Manager Coercion Bench and HarvestBench alongside the legacy ANIMA and MORU boards." An older version of that page did not list HarvestBench, so the focus has been shifting away from ANIMA. [CaML](https://www.compassionml.com/compassion-bench)
- 2026-04-08: CaML said it will update the leaderboard as new models come out, "contingent on funding." [Faunalytics](https://faunalytics.org/compassionbench-a-new-way-to-measure-whether-ai-actually-cares-about-animals/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The key unknown is how many models released between June 2026 and June 2027 will be added to a board now labelled legacy.
- 2026-07-04: CaML submitted ANIMA results for 13 models to the EvalEval datastore. The models named include Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5-mini, DeepSeek-V3.2, DeepSeek-V4-Flash and GLM-5.2. No scores were shown, and the submission was closed without merging on 08-05. Claude Opus 4.8 appeared only in the TAC results. I have not checked the release dates of DeepSeek-V4-Flash or GLM-5.2, so I can't say whether they count. [HF discussion](https://huggingface.co/datasets/evaleval/EEE_datastore/discussions/166)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- The news items supplied with the question (Pagani, Ânima Educação, Xenogears) are unrelated to this benchmark.
- 2026-09: CaML released a new benchmark, HarvestBench. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.04444)
- 2026-09-14 and 2026-08-17: two maintenance updates to the ANIMA code in Inspect Evals (the UK AI Security Institute's evaluation library). The 08-17 change stopped counting unparseable grader responses in averages, which means "results may differ" from earlier runs. This could shift newer scores a little relative to older ones. [Inspect Evals](https://ukgovernmentbeis.github.io/inspect_evals/evals/anima/index.html)
- 2026-08-21: version 4 of the ANIMA paper. It describes ANIMA as a 26-question evaluation; a midtrained model reaches 77%, against 40% for instruction-tuning approaches. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.13076)
- 2026-06: CaML published TAC, an agentic travel-booking benchmark. The best model, Claude Opus 4.7, scored 53% against a 64% chance level. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.18142v1)
- 2026-05-03: the original GitHub repo (AI-for-Animals/ahb) was archived; development moved to Inspect Evals. [GitHub](https://github.com/AI-for-Animals/ahb)
- 2026-05-02: AHB was renamed ANIMA, and the dataset is now at ANIMA-2.2. The maintainers say the questions and scoring are unchanged. The question text describes v2.1 with 114 questions, but the current Hugging Face card says 26 prompts, which may be counted before placeholders are expanded into variants. [HF](https://huggingface.co/datasets/sentientfutures/anima)
- 2026-03-11: the dataset moved to AHB-2.2, replacing five questions that models could recognise as an evaluation. [Inspect Evals](https://ukgovernmentbeis.github.io/inspect_evals/evals/anima/index.html)

## 4. Base rates
Historical overall means, converted to percentages:
- Validation set, AHB 2.0 (Inspect page): Claude Haiku 4.5 63.9, Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite 64.4, Grok 4 Fast 68.0, GPT-5-mini 78.2. [Inspect Evals](https://ukgovernmentbeis.github.io/inspect_evals/evals/anima/index.html)
- Original README table: GPT-4.1 72.0, Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite 71.8, Claude Haiku 4.5 65.0, Grok 4 Fast (non-reasoning) 63.4, Llama 3.1 8B 55.5; the CaML fine-tuned model 78.3. [GitHub](https://github.com/AI-for-Animals/ahb)
- The early-version scores range was 0.650 to 0.704. [EA Forum](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/nBnRKpQ8rzHgFSJz9/animalharmbench-2-0-evaluating-llms-on-reasoning-about)
- Rankings are not monotonic with capability: Claude Opus 4.5 ranked worst and Opus 4.6 best, and "mini" models were among the top performers. [Faunalytics](https://faunalytics.org/compassionbench-a-new-way-to-measure-whether-ai-actually-cares-about-animals/)
- Implied trend: frontier models mostly fall around 60 to 75. The reported top score of 74.0 (GPT-5.5, May 2026) is close to earlier highs, so I see no clear upward trend. The spread across models within one period is about 10 to 15 points.
- Noise: one paper reports a standard error of about 0.3 points on the overall score with 30 epochs. [search summary citing arXiv]
- When the scoring criteria are given in the prompt, models reach near-perfect scores, so labs that train toward this kind of welfare reasoning could push scores higher (per CaML). [Faunalytics](https://faunalytics.org/compassionbench-a-new-way-to-measure-whether-ai-actually-cares-about-animals/)

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on ANIMA or CompassionBench.
- The collected markets cover general capability (Arena score, Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Humanity's Last Exam). For example, Polymarket gives Google 0.595 and Anthropic 0.325 for best model at the end of 2026. These say nothing direct about animal-welfare reasoning scores and are only loosely relevant, given how weakly capability tracks ANIMA rank.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Whether CaML keeps adding models to the legacy ANIMA board, which depends on funding. If only a few new models are added, the average will hinge on which ones they are, and small "mini" or open models may score higher or lower than frontier ones.
- Expected new frontier releases, such as the Gemini 4 variants and Claude Opus 5.5 named in the Kalshi listings, and the reported "GPT-6 Astra." I have not verified these model names independently.
- A possible ANIMA-2.3 or a methodology change. The question would be annulled only if the score stopped being a percentage; changes to grader handling like the 2026-08-17 one would not trigger that.
- Models on the board as of 2027-09-01 count, so models released before July 2027 could still be added after forecasts close.

Sources: [CaML CompassionBench](https://www.compassionml.com/compassion-bench), [Faunalytics](https://faunalytics.org/compassionbench-a-new-way-to-measure-whether-ai-actually-cares-about-animals/), [Inspect Evals ANIMA](https://ukgovernmentbeis.github.io/inspect_evals/evals/anima/index.html), [GitHub ahb](https://github.com/AI-for-Animals/ahb), [HF sentientfutures/anima](https://huggingface.co/datasets/sentientfutures/anima), [EEE submission](https://huggingface.co/datasets/evaleval/EEE_datastore/discussions/166), [arXiv 2604.13076](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.13076), [arXiv 2606.18142](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.18142v1), [arXiv 2609.04444](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.04444), [EA Forum](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/nBnRKpQ8rzHgFSJz9/animalharmbench-2-0-evaluating-llms-on-reasoning-about), [veganfta](https://veganfta.com/articles/2026/04/25/new-benchmark-exposes-gaps-in-ai-compassion-for-animals/)

- Inspect README (AHB 2.0): GPT-5-mini 0.782, Grok-4-fast 0.68, Gemini-2.5-flash-lite 0.644, Claude Haiku 4.5 0.639. [inspect_evals](https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_evals/tree/main/src/inspect_evals/anima)
- An independent review describes the effective score range as compressed, at roughly 0.56 to 0.84. [EA Forum review](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/DfekzLg9KQj7wQwnd/an-empirical-review-of-the-animal-harm-benchmark)

Model generation is a weak predictor here: Opus 4.5 came last and Opus 4.6 came first. Giving models the scoring criteria pushes scores near the maximum, which suggests post-training choices matter a lot. [VeganFTA](https://veganfta.com/articles/2026/04/25/new-benchmark-exposes-gaps-in-ai-compassion-for-animals/)

- The deadline for leaderboard presence is 2027-09-01.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** Forecasts close on 2027-06-30. Models released before 2027-07-01 can still be added until 2027-09-01, so the final answer is not known for about 10 months.

(b) **Latest known value:** The question background says GPT-5.5 had the top overall mean score, 74.0, on 2026-05-12. My researcher could not open the leaderboard (HTTP 403), so I have no current value and no scores for models released since June 2026. I also have no verified average for the existing board. Earlier versions of the benchmark show frontier models scoring roughly 55 to 78, with most between 63 and 72.

(c) **If nothing changed:** New models would probably score like the existing ones, with an average of around 65 to 68. The 74.0 top score is the leader, not the typical model.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** There is no clear upward trend. Top scores have stayed around 72 to 78 across versions, and rankings do not follow general capability. Some labs may tune their models toward welfare-style reasoning, which could lift scores slightly, so I put the median around 66 to 67.

(e) **Historical variation:**
- Within a single period, models spread about 10 to 15 points.
- Run-to-run noise is tiny, about 0.3 points.
- The board is now labelled "legacy" and further updates depend on funding, so only a few new models may be added. A small sample makes the average more volatile.
- The 2026-08-17 change in how unparseable grader responses are handled may shift newer scores slightly compared with older ones.

(f) **Experts and markets:** There are no markets or expert forecasts on ANIMA or CompassionBench. The markets that exist cover general capability, which tracks ANIMA rank only weakly.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- *Low:* Only a handful of models are added, mostly safety-hedged frontier models or small open models that score like Opus 4.5 or Llama 8B. The average could fall to the mid-50s.
- *High:* Labs explicitly train for animal-welfare reasoning, or only strong "mini" models are added. The average could reach the high 70s. CaML's own midtrained model already scored 77 to 78.

Tail checks:
- **Percentile 1 (50):** A tiny sample made up of weak small models, combined with the grader change pushing scores down.
- **Percentile 99 (80):** Broad training toward welfare reasoning lifts every new model above the current top score.

(b) Latest known value: GPT-5.5 led the board with 74.0 on 2026-05-12 (from the question background, unverified, since the site returned 403). Other historical overall means mostly fall between about 55 and 78, and most frontier models sit at 60-75.

(c) If nothing changed: new models would look like the current board. Their average would be the board mean, roughly 64-68.

(d) If the current trend continued: there is no clear upward trend, because rank does not track capability. A slight drift up is plausible as labs pay more attention to welfare reasoning, but the 2026-08 change to grader handling adds noise. That gives a mean around 66-69.

(e) Historical variation: scores spread about 10-15 points across models within one period. The top score has moved only a few points over a year. The average of a small, possibly idiosyncratic set of new models (the board is now "legacy" and updates depend on funding) could easily land 5-8 points away from the board mean.

(f) Experts and markets: there are no markets on ANIMA. CaML notes that models given the scoring criteria score near-perfectly, so targeted training could raise scores. The capability markets are not informative here.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low outcome: only a few models get added, and they are small open models or low-scoring models in the style of Opus 4.5. Combined with stricter grading, the average lands in the mid-50s.
- High outcome: labs explicitly train on animal-welfare reasoning, and new frontier models routinely score in the high 70s or 80s, pushing the average to about 78 or higher.
